description: Cofounded by Twitter’s Jack Dorsey in 2009, Block has expanded from its initial point-of-sale company, Square, to offer a suite of products ranging from music streaming to Bitcoin mining. Dorsey previously split his time between Square and Twitter before resigning from the social media platform in 2021 and renaming the company Block that same year. While Square remains the conglomerate’s core business, its other flagship products include Cash App, a consumer payments rival to Venmo and Zelle, as well as Tidal, which competes against Spotify. Driven by Dorsey, Block also operates in the crypto space, including creating Bitcoin hardware wallets under the Bitkey brand.

title: Block

rankings.title: The Future 50
rankings.itemDescription: The fintech company formerly known as Square has been growing rapidly on the strength of its services for merchants—including credit card payment processing and data analytics—and its CashApp peer-to-peer payment tool. Net profits remain elusive as the company invests in building and marketing new features, but Block is still on pace to top $20 billion in revenue in 2023.

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in Financial Services and Insurance
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

“Square is truly the best company that I've ever worked for in my career. There is a shared sense of pride and responsibility around virtually everything that we do. Our People team and executives truly care about doing the right thing and building something that will far outlive each of us. There's no fear that prevents us from taking principled risks, and we are not afraid to experiment and try new things. We are a collection of the kind of people that can change the world.”

rankings.title: Best Large Workplaces in the Bay Area
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

“Management is generally very transparent and makes a good-faith effort to address any employee concerns. The most unique aspect is how open they are with providing safe spaces to discuss cultural or political events that impact people's lives outside of work. They understand that it's sometimes unreasonable to expect people to compartmentalize their emotional or personal selves and leave that at home, and are willing to have difficult conversations about a variety of issues.”

rankings.title: 100 Best Large Workplaces for Millennials
rankings.itemDescription:
Employees say:

“The culture of work-life balance. People are free to be who they are and interact in a way that is personable, but not forced. People of all different backgrounds and personalities are hired and encouraged to be themselves and bring their unique talents to the table. In terms of work-life balance, I've never worked somewhere that employees are encouraged to take time for themselves when they need it. The company talks the talk but also walks the walk. It's amazing and I feel privileged to be part of it.”

rankings.title: Fortune 500
rankings.itemDescription: The digital payments company runs two main businesses: point-of-sale technology for small and medium businesses, including its flagship Square Reader, and the Cash App, which features peer-to-peer financial transactions and cryptocurrency trading. In March, Square reached an agreement to acquire majority ownership in streaming service Tidal, and in May, the company announced it was expanding into Ireland. Square's first quarter 2021 report showed revenue increased more than 200% year over year.

rankings.title: The Future 50
rankings.itemDescription: Square, which was once best known for its little white plug-in credit card swipers—as well as being Twitter CEO Jack Dorsey’s side hustle—has grown into a major force in payments and banking in its own right. With a stock price that has tripled so far in 2020, Square’s market value has surpassed that of Goldman Sachs. What has investors so revved up? Likely its shiny new banking license (approved in March) and its Cash App, a peer-to-peer payments and cryptocurrency-trading service whose rapid growth has made it a rival to PayPal’s Venmo. Next up: a possible acquisition of Credit Karma’s tax-preparation business.
